text:
Priya Singh: Hey team — CS escalated a customer (standard plan) hitting intermittent 429s on POST /v1/completions when they burst ~25-35 reqs/s for ~40s. They’re seeing retries from our JS SDK and suspect duplicate side-effects (duplicate DB rows / invoices). Logs attached by customer show request ids and a bunch of 429s then 200s for the same payload.

Ethan Cole: Do we have their rate-limit headers captured? X-RateLimit-Remaining / Retry-After?

Priya Singh: They provided this snippet from their logs: `x-ratelimit-limit: 100`, `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, `retry-after: 1.2`. They weren’t sending an Idempotency-Key. They relied on SDK defaults (`retries: 3` in JS SDK) and used the convenience `client.createCompletion()` call.

Mateo Rivera: Two quick things: (1) If the endpoint is non-idempotent (creates), retries can cause duplicates unless the caller provides an idempotency token. (2) 429 handling is subtle — some clients retry automatically on 429, others don't. Our SDK currently retries on network errors and 5xx, and has limited 429 logic.

Priya Singh: Customer wants guidance and a repro we can run. Also worried the SDK defaults are surprising.

Ethan Cole: Repro steps to ask customer:
• Exact request pattern (payload + concurrency + interval)
• Whether they reuse a connection (keep-alive)
• Full response headers for a failing request (trace-id, retry-after)
• Example request body so we can reproduce side-effect semantics

Support Bot: trace_id=tr_4b9c2a — quota hit observed at 2026-11-12T15:42:17Z, shard=us-west-2

Mateo Rivera: Recommended immediate guidance to customer:
• Add an Idempotency-Key header for create/charge-like ops. Example:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"prompt":"…"}'
```

• Implement exponential backoff with full jitter. Example algorithm (pseudocode):

```
base = 300ms
attempt = 0
sleep = min(cap, base * 2^attempt)
sleep = random_between(0, sleep)
attempt += 1
```

• Respect Retry-After when present for 429s.

Priya Singh: For the SDK defaults proposal: customer-facing docs should call out that non-idempotent endpoints require callers to supply Idempotency-Key to avoid duplicates. Also propose we change JS SDK to:
• Default to not automatically retry POST-like endpoints on 429 unless an Idempotency-Key is present.
• If Idempotency-Key present, allow safe retries for 429/5xx using exponential backoff + jitter (cap 10s, max attempts 5).

Ethan Cole: Agree. Also add telemetry to record when SDK retries on 429 so we can see how common this is.

Mateo Rivera: Quick internal checklist for us:
1) Reproduce with a local load test hitting /v1/completions at 30 req/s for 60s with no idempotency header. Capture any duplicated side-effects in a test harness.
2) Verify server returns consistent idempotency semantics when Idempotency-Key provided.
3) Add a KB article for CS explaining safe retry patterns and sample code for Node/Python/Go.
4) Patch JS SDK to gate 429 retries on Idempotency-Key and update defaults/docs.

Priya Singh: Action for CS: ask customer to (a) add Idempotency-Key to create calls, (b) enable debug logs and send first/failed request headers, (c) if they want, we can run a controlled repro against a sandbox token.

Ethan Cole: Minor note — some customers spike because of client-side bursting (e.g., retry storms). Recommend they add a client-side token bucket limiter (burst window ~5s) to smooth traffic.

Priya Singh: I'll reply to the customer with those steps and open an internal ticket for the SDK change + KB. Marking as P1 until we confirm duplicate billing side-effects.

Support Bot: Ticket created: #INC-2026-4589 — assigned to eng-runtime for reproduction.
